name: Apeeye
use_label: Spin up mock REST endpoints fast
one_liner: Mock REST endpoints in seconds — no login, no config, no database.

text.why: Building the screen before the backend exists usually stalls. In Apeeye you name a collection and it is a live endpoint immediately — callable from your app, from curl or Postman, or from a teammate’s machine.
text.take: It states the trade-off outright: close the tab and callers get a clear 503. A clean stop is less confusing than something half alive.
build: Records live only in your browser’s IndexedDB; the server stores nothing. A stateless relay forwards each request over a WebSocket to your open tab, which answers from IndexedDB. GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE all work with sensible status codes, and a whole workspace exports and imports as JSON. You can also clone it and run it locally.

who.role: Front-end developers waiting on a backend, and anyone who needs a throwaway API for a demo or a class.

start.text: Open the Playground at apeeye.ibr0r.com, add a collection such as users, and call the workspace URL shown at the top.

caveat: The endpoints answer only while a tab is open. There are no accounts, so anyone with the workspace URL can read and write it — keep real data out. It is an early project with single-digit stars.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
